To: Emma Zhao <emma@datawave.ai>; Luke Chen <luke.chen@retailco.com>

Subject: Reranker integration & eval follow-up — next steps and tech deep-dive

Hi Emma / Luke —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: integrate Redwood’s reranker to improve query result relevance for your help-center + product search use cases (reduce time-to-answer for customers and boost conversion for product queries).
- MVP success metrics (we discussed): relative NDCG@10 uplift >= 10% over baseline; MRR improvement; acceptable p95 latency <= 200ms for single-item rerank (budgeted target).
- Integrations: candidate retrieval will remain in your infra (Elastic + sparse retriever). Redwood will provide a /rank endpoint that accepts a list of candidates + query and returns ordered scores. We suggested a top_k (default 10) for initial rollouts.

Action items / owners: 
1) Marissa: share post-call notes + sample eval queries (attached).
2) Dev: provide SDK snippet, auth options, and evaluation guidance (Dev to propose parameters: top_k, score-normalization, batch size).
3) DataWave (Emma): share a small dev dataset (50–200 query/candidate groups) and confirm a 1-hour tech deep-dive on Tue.
4) Rishi/Vivek: prepare a quick pricing sketch for a dedicated reranker tier if we need higher throughput/SLA.

I attached the post-call notes and a tiny sample CSV you can use for the dry-run. If this looks good, let’s lock the Tue tech session (I suggested Tue 10:00 PST in the call).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Reranker integration & eval follow-up — next steps and tech deep-dive

All — adding the technical sketch and an SDK example below. I also attached a short spec with payload examples.

High-level reranker API (v1):
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> (we also support mTLS for Private deployments)
Payload (JSON): {
  "query": "...",
  "candidates": [ {"id":"c1","text":"..."}, {"id":"c2","text":"..."} ],
  "top_k": 10,
  "return_scores": true,
  "structured_output": false
}
Response:
{ "ranked": [ {"id":"c2","score":0.92}, {"id":"c1","score":0.73} ], "timing_ms": 78 }

Notes and tuning knobs: 
- top_k: controls how many returned results we re-order. For your use-case start with 10; evaluate NDCG@10 and NDCG@5.
- batch mode: you can send up to 16 query groups per request for throughput. Batching increases throughput but may increase tail latency.
- embeddings + reranker: typical pattern is retrieval-first (your existing retriever -> top 100 candidates), then rerank top_k (10–20) with the reranker. If you want to use embeddings to pre-filter, we can provide a simple scoring function in our SDK.
- scoring: returned scores are monotonic but not calibrated across models — for A/B we recommend using relative rank metrics (NDCG/MRR) rather than raw score thresholds.
- eval: upload your sample CSV (query, ground_truth_ids, candidate_pool) and we’ll run offline NDCG/MRR and a latency/cost simulation.

SDK example (Python):

import requests
API_KEY = "REDACTED"
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank"
payload = {
  "query": "How do I reset my API token?",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "To reset, go to settings > tokens..."},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "You can rotate tokens under account > security..."}
  ],
  "top_k": 5,
  "return_scores": True
}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"})
print(resp.json())

Attached: reranker_api_spec.md with payloads, rate limits, and example NDCG calculation script.

[Attachment: reranker_api_spec.md (MD, 12KB)]

On the evaluation side, here’s what I recommend for your 2-stage plan: 
A) Offline validation (week 1): run NDCG@10, MRR, Precision@1 on your sample set. Compute significance (paired t-test / bootstrap) vs your baseline. B) Canary rollout (week 2): small percentage of traffic with live logging to compare click-through/retrieval success. C) Full rollout with auto-fallback to baseline model if MRR drops > X%.

Happy to walk through the spec in the Tue deep-dive.

—Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.ai

From: Emma Zhao <emma@datawave.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reranker integration & eval follow-up — next steps and tech deep-dive

Thanks Marissa and Dev — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before the deep-dive: 

1) Candidate pool size: we typically retrieve top 200 from our Elastic index. You recommended reranking top_k=10 after retrieval; is it worth doing a small experiment reranking top_k=20 to see returns for long-tail queries?

2) Ground truth labeling: our internal labeling is noisy — do you have recommendations for de-duplicating and handling ambiguous labels in NDCG computation?

3) Latency budget: 200ms p95 is tight for us. Can you confirm the expected contribution of the reranker to end-to-end latency (given retrieval is ~90ms)? Also, do you support GPU-backed dedicated pools for lower latency?

We’ll attach a small sample dataset tonight.

—Emma
Emma Zhao
Head of Product, DataWave Analytics
emma@datawave.ai

On Mon, 2 Mar 2026 at 10:55:00 -0800, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai> wrote:

Emma — quick note on pricing and rollout tiers: 
- If you go hosted (shared), reranker pricing will be usage-based per-ranked-group + token estimate. For predictable latency we can propose Dedicated Reranker Pools (monthly commit).
- For the pilot the hosted plan is fine; if performance tests look promising we’ll surface a Dedicated quote in the follow-up.

I’ll bring a short pricing slide to Tue’s session.

—Rishi Malhotra
Principal Sales | Redwood Inference
